newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Observers, big investors and fund managers in the Egyptian market agree that the price rally which started last week was the end of the correction which began at the beginning of March.
- Eastern Company and Alexandria Spinning and Weaving/Spinalex have put their shares in the central depositary, bringing the number of companies which have done so to a total of 15.

- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib said that at the end of May or beginning of June the government will take a decision to issue Egyptian pound bonds abroad. Four institutions have offered to arrange issues of bonds with maturity between three and five years with a yield of 9.25 percent.

- Ahmed el-Edwi, the managing director of Nile Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries said the new management which took over at the end of last year has managed to improve working methods and increase company profits. The company made 12.606 million pounds ($3.71 million) profits before tax and before auditing in the first seven months (July-January) of the financial year, compared with 18.783 million in the same period of 1995/6. But the company expects net year-end profits of 30 million pounds and a dividend of 6.76 pounds a share.

- Arab Drugs and Chemical Industries made net profits of 5.96 million pounds before tax and before auditing in the first seven months of the year 1996/7, compared with 6.19 million in the same period of the previous year.

- Some of the subsidiaries which the state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories plans to sell to anchor investors made low profits relative to assets. Egyptian Refractories, for example, made 261,000 pounds in the six months ending December, compared with 1.6 million in the same period of 1995/6.

- Egyptian Electro Cables made a surplus on current operations of 13.1 million pounds in the first six months of the financial year, compared with 6.3 million in the same period of the previous year. Sales were worth 157.9 million pounds in the period, compared with 164.7 million in the same period of 1995/6.

- American Express Bank has received applications for units worth more than 400 million pounds in its new mutual fund. The bank had raised the maximum to 300 million from 100 million. It will continue to accept applications until Tuesday.
